newsitem.title: POLAND: World Bank chief says policy on Belarus unchanged.
newsitem.headline: World Bank chief says policy on Belarus unchanged.

text.p: Plans for a union between Russia and Belarus have not affected the World Bank's policy towards either country, the bank's President James Wolfensohn said on Friday.
Wolfensohn was asked at a news conference in Warsaw what impact the charter on forming a union between the two former Soviet republics might have on World Bank assistance to them.
He recalled that he had met all the top Russian leaders in Moscow last month, when he proposed lending the country $6 billion over two years with an emphasis on social programmes.
"We never mentioned Belarus as an issue in terms of financial assistance," Wolfensohn said.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin hopes to meet Belarus leader Alexander Lukashenko on May 23 to sign a charter on forming a union, a plan which enjoys both wide support and some strong opposition in both countries.

Belarus nationalists accuse Russia of imperialistic plans while Russian liberals are cautious about drawing closer to the hardline Lukashenko and fear union with Belarus, where economic reforms are at an embryonic stage, could slow Russia's move to a full market economy and become a financial burden.
Such concerns led to a union treaty signed by Yeltsin and Lukashenko on April 2 being watered down.
Wolfensohn said that if any World Bank officials had spoken about any impact of the proposed treaty, he himself had not.

"I can deny that it is an issue -- it is a consideration which needs to be watched but it has not affected our policy (towards Russia) and, so far as I know, it has not affected our policy towards Belarus," he said.
Wolfensohn said that whenever there were arrangements between countries the impact had to be assessed.
"But we have not made any negative assessment that I am aware of, so I would not assume there has been any change in bank policy," he added.
